title: [Autour de La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois, pages 1 à 67] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context (continuing from p.121). L/K is a function field and 𝒳 = lim← X is the Zariski–Riemann space: the inverse limit of all proper (here projective) models X of L over K. Each point x ∈ 𝒳 has a local ring 𝒪_{𝒳,x} = colim 𝒪_{X,x_X}. The Proposition on the previous page states that 𝒪_{𝒳,x} is a valuation ring of L containing K with fraction field L, and that x ↦ 𝒪_{𝒳,x} is a bijection onto the set of such rings. This is Zariski's theorem.

Top of this page: the end of part (a) of the proof. Take f ∈ L, written as f = g/h with g, h ∈ 𝒪_{X,x} on some projective model X. By resolution of singularities, after further blow-ups one may assume X is regular at x and that g, h are monomials in a regular system of parameters. Cancelling common factors makes g, h 'coprime'. Blowing up further, one makes the divisors of g and h separate near x. Then, at the image of x, either g | h or h | g, so f or 1/f lies in 𝒪_{𝒳,x}. This is the valuation property. (Bijectivity, part (a) continued, is left implicit.)

Part (b) sketches how a covering (finite étale, or tame, cover) relative to the extension L/K is determined. One takes x ∈ 𝒳 and passes to the 'local' object at x, i.e. the localisation 𝒪_{𝒳,x} or the pro-system of neighbourhoods U_{𝒳,x}. The covering is then a limit of coverings of models U of L/K defined over neighbourhoods of the images of x.

NB, partly crossed out. The transforms of 𝒳 in a proper model X are clear. Models of L/K (not necessarily proper) correspond to certain open subsets of 𝒳. These are not all quasi-compact opens / not stable under finite operations.

Last lines: the generalisation to an arbitrary (normal?) local ring O ⊂ L with fraction field L. One takes its normalisation O' in L̄ (the separable or algebraic closure of L), and for x' over x the decomposition group D_{x'} and inertia group I_{x'}. The interpretations given earlier for 'jauge' rings (divisorial-type valuations) are thereby extended. The next page pursues this: for a valuation of 'rank' (cardinal) α one expects inertia groups with a filtered or simplicial structure T^α. This is the Galois-theoretic encoding of the points of 𝒳 for birational anabelian purposes.
errors: The proof of the valuation property via resolution of singularities and monomialization is heavy overkill. It is also unavailable in positive characteristic in dimension > 3. The elementary argument suffices: replace X by the closure of the graph of the rational map f: X ⇢ P^1, i.e. blow up the ideal (g,h). At the point of this model lying under x, either f or 1/f is regular. This is Zariski's original argument.
The proof given is only a sketch. The 'separation of divisors' step and the injectivity/surjectivity of x ↦ 𝒪_{𝒳,x} are not written out.

ideas.what: The Zariski–Riemann space 𝒳 = lim of proper models, with points corresponding bijectively to valuation rings of L/K
ideas.where_published: Not in EGA as such; EGA II §7 treats valuative criteria

ideas.what: Proving the valuation property via resolution: monomialize g, h and blow up until their divisors separate
ideas.modern_name: Principalization / monomialization of a pair of functions

ideas.what: Open subsets of the Zariski–Riemann space correspond to (non-proper) models of L/K
ideas.modern_name: Topology of the Riemann–Zariski space; models as opens

ideas.what: Decomposition and inertia groups in Gal(L̄/L) attached to points of the Zariski–Riemann space (arbitrary valuations of L/K); a structure on inertia reflecting the rank of the valuation
ideas.modern_name: Valuation-theoretic decomposition/inertia groups; local theory in birational anabelian geometry
ideas.usually_credited_to: Classical (Hilbert, Krull); anabelian use by Pop (1990s), Bogomolov–Tschinkel
ideas.where_published: Ideas around birational anabelian geometry in Esquisse d'un programme and the letter to Faltings (1983); La Longue Marche itself is unpublished

missed.claim: Grothendieck sets up the Zariski–Riemann space of L/K as the natural 'space of points' indexing decomposition and inertia subgroups of the absolute Galois group of a function field. He intends to read off the rank of the valuation from the structure of inertia. This anticipates Pop's local theory recovering valuations, and their rank, from Galois groups. It is consistent with what is known of Grothendieck's birational anabelian ideas, so it is probably not new to specialists.

missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Historical: it documents that Grothendieck in c.1981 already framed birational anabelian local theory via the Riemann–Zariski space.

deep.surprise_reason: Mostly a standard proof (Zariski's theorem, done with heavier tools than needed) plus the set-up of decomposition/inertia groups for general valuations. The anabelian orientation is known to be Grothendieck's, and no finished new result is visible.
transcription_corrections: '(pas stables par dimension finie)' is more likely '(pas stables par intersection finie)' or similar, referring to opens of 𝒳.
'b) Un revêtement de url V' is likely 'b) Un revêtement de un V' or 'Un revêtement d'un V', i.e. a covering of an open V.
'donné U_{𝒳,x}' is likely the underlined local object 𝒪_{𝒳,x}.
'Pour H anneau local?' is likely 'Pour A anneau local?' (O ⊂ L), with 'normal?' inserted above.
The crossed-out text before 'dans un modèle propre X' is approximately '(ceux qui viennent ...'.
'des diviseurs de f, g ... se séparent' is consistent with the image; the first line is likely 'en un ou plusieurs (pas)' / 'monômes en un ...'.
